title: Being Brave
passages: Courage is not the same as having no fear. Being brave often means feeling your heart pound and choosing to keep going anyway. A brave person might feel shaky, unsure, or worried, and still take one small step forward. Courage can be loud, like standing up for a friend, but it is often quiet and PERSISTENT, like trying again after something feels hard. Sometimes the bravest thing is letting yourself feel VULNERABLE and being honest about how you feel. Every person carries their own kind of courage inside them, even on days when it feels very small.

Small brave things happen everywhere, every single day. Someone tries a new food, says hello to a stranger, or asks for help when they need it. In a busy market in a faraway city, a child might bargain with a shopkeeper for the very first time. In a quiet village, someone might sing in front of their whole community, feeling nervous and proud at once. People in every corner of the world find their own ways to show RESILIENCE. Waiting patiently, forgiving a friend, or sharing a new idea can all take courage. Each small act builds CONFIDENCE, one moment at a time.
